questions.prompt: In Anthropic's terms, what makes a system an agent rather than a workflow?

options.text: It uses more than one tool.
options.explanation: Workflows use tools too. The difference is who picks the next step.

options.text: The model directs its own process and tool use.
options.explanation: Right. Workflows follow predefined code paths; agents dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage.

options.text: It keeps a conversation history across turns.
options.explanation: A workflow can keep history too. What matters is who picks the next step: your code or the model.

questions.prompt: The OpenAI Agents SDK runner gets output from the model. Which output makes it switch agents and continue?

options.explanation: Right. The runner switches to that agent and keeps looping.

options.text: A final answer with no more tool work
options.explanation: That ends the run and returns a result.
The runner executes the tools and continues with the same agent.

questions.prompt: An agent has run 20 turns in one session. What do the Claude docs say about its context window?

options.text: It resets after every turn, so only the last result is kept.
options.explanation: The docs say the context window does not reset between turns within a session.

options.text: It only holds the system prompt and the user's first message.
options.explanation: Tool inputs and tool outputs are added every turn as well.

options.text: It holds everything so far: prompt, tools, history, tool inputs and outputs.
options.explanation: Right. Everything accumulates, which is why long tool outputs and long sessions get expensive.
